summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and StrataForge to explore a channel/reseller onramp + GPU cloud interop. Discussed deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance gating, pilot plan for benchmarks, and integration patterns for VPC routing and KMS. Customer is interested in predictable latency for low-latency inference and easier reseller billing flow.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-31 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~56 mins | Recording: yes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (StrataForge), Tomás (Infra), Elise (Security), Jonah (Pre-sales)

[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you squeezing this in. quick round robin intro?
[00:18] Maya (StrataForge): sure, i'm maya, head of cloud partnerships at StrataForge. we do a managed gpu cloud for edge SaaS partners and channel resellers.
[00:28] Tomás (StrataForge): tomás infra, i run the networking and infra architecture.
[00:32] Elise (StrataForge): elise, security. i'll be the main reviewer for compliance.
[00:37] Jonah: jonah on pre-sales, help scope pilots.
[00:41] Diego (Redwood SE): diego, i'm the se, i'll dig into latency/benchmarks and integration patterns.
[00:46] Ava: awesome. high-level goal — figure out if an onramp integration makes sense: routing Redwood-hosted requests through StrataForge capacity, or letting customers use Redwood Dedicated on top of your GPU pools.
[01:05] Maya: yes ideally we want a flow where our customers can buy capacity via StrataForge and we handle billing, but we need easy routing and a clear security model.
[01:18] Tomás: technical constraints — we run mixed gpu fleet (A100 and some H100s coming), kubernetes based, and we do VPC peering or private link for partners. wondering how Redwood handles private deployments — is it a control plane that stays with you or can we host the control plane?
[01:42] Diego: good question. Redwood's private option can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane or a hosted control plane with VPC connectivity. we call it Redwood Private, sometimes clients refer to it as Redwoods Private or 'private control plane' — sorry transcription note. for channel/reseller we often do a thin control plane that is customer- or partner-managed for audit reasons.
[02:05] Elise: from security perspective we need to see SOC2 + ISO27001. also KMS integrations for key management, and HSM support is preferred. how do you handle tokenization and logs?
[02:20] Diego: we support KMS integrations and can integrate with partner KMS via cross-account roles, plus optional HSM. audit logs can be streamed to partner S3/secure storage per routing policy. note: sometimes our export formatting is called 'audit stream' in docs.
[02:39] Maya: latency is a big deal for many customers — typical completion latency target is under 150ms for 512 tokens. can you meet that on pooled capacity?
[02:51] Diego: depends on batching, quantization, and the model. for small sequence lengths and continuous KV caching we can get 40-120ms on H100/A100 with optimized kernels; on heavier batching it can drift. we need a sample workload to be sure.
[03:08] Tomás: for billing/reseller flow we will need metering hooks — per-token or per-response counters. can Redwood expose per-customer usage metrics for us to ingest?
[03:21] Ava: yes we expose token-level metering and per-route breakdowns. we can publish a pull API or push webhooks for usage to your billing system. we prefer push for near-real-time billing.
[03:34] Jonah: in terms of partner program, are there incentives or margin splits?
[03:39] Ava: that's more of a GTM question — i'll loop in partnerships for the formal program, but technically the flow is straightforward.
[03:48] Maya: on the integration pattern, we want to avoid double egress across clouds. can you support colocated routing (i.e., Redwood routing inside our VPC so traffic doesn't leave)?
[04:02] Diego: yes, via private peering and control plane proxies we can route traffic internally — we call it vpc egress bypass internally but docs may say 'private route'. network setup will require a small NAT/proxy inside your k8s cluster.
[04:22] Tomás: how would model failover work? say your hosted pool is saturated, can it fallback to Redwood Dedicated or a cheaper model?
[04:33] Diego: smart routing policies — policy based on latency/cost/region. automatic fallback to compatible model variants is possible; for example, fall back from 70B quantized to 13B for cost/latency. we'll surface those as routes in the config.
[04:51] Elise: auditability — we need immutable logs and request replay. is that possible?
[04:58] Diego: yes, request traces and token-level logs can be exported. request replay has caveats for PII; we'd expect redaction or hashed payloads for replay.
[05:12] Maya: pilot idea — run a small benchmark of 1000 requests across 3 models (small/medium/large) to measure p95 latency and tokens per USD on your engine vs our local pool. can Redwood provide a standard benchmark harness?
[05:27] Diego: yes i'll share a lightweight harness (python and k6 scripts) — it's what we use internally. it includes warm/cold starts, KV cache priming, and quantization toggle.
[05:40] Tomás: GPU SKUs — we currently prefer H100 for low latency, but A100 is fine if cost is lower. any quantization workarounds for H100?
[05:53] Diego: quantization works across SKUs but there are kernel differences — sometimes H100 benefits from bf16 paths, we also have int8 for A100 in some models. there is an internal note where we referred to H100 as H1O0 in a deck — ignore that.
[06:08] Maya: security checklist: SSO (SAML), SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC, per-tenant encryption keys. can you integrate with our SAML IdP and do SCIM?
[06:20] Ava: yep, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported; RBAC is role-based and configurable via console or API.
[06:27] Elise: data residency — some customers need EU-only. can routing be region-locked?
[06:33] Diego: yes policies can pin to region and model variants. we call it smart routing in docs.
[06:40] Jonah: curious about developer experience — how much code change for our customers?
[06:46] Ava: minimal. most call flows stay the same; they change endpoint or add partner header. we provide SDK snippets for node/python and a migration doc.
[06:58] Maya: what about autoscaling? our load can be spiky. do you do bursts into shared capacity?
[07:06] Diego: Redwood Dedicated has burst capacity options and autoscaling policies. you can reserve baseline and allow burst to hosted pool. for channel flows we can map bursts to a fallback model or queue with priority.
[07:21] Tomás: network egress — if we host model weights locally, what's the control plane chat like? do we ever push weights across public internet?
[07:30] Diego: weights are typically stored in secure artifact stores inside the VPC. control plane commands can be proxied over private peering. we avoid pushing weights over public net for private deployments.
[07:42] Maya: pricing model — per-token + reserved capacity. can we get a partner price sheet?
[07:49] Ava: yes i'll send a partner pricing template. we'll include reserved capacity tiers and per-token typical ranges.
[07:56] Elise: about legal/compliance — we need an NDA and also a minimal MSA draft for pilot. can you share?
[08:03] Ava: yep i will attach NDA and a pilot SOW template. legal will follow for MSA.
[08:10] Tomás: do you do compliance scans in our infra? like CIS or other benchmarks?
[08:17] Diego: we can run a checklist and add an ops onboarding where we validate network and k8s configurations. we sometimes call that a 'ramp' in internal docs.
[08:30] (brief cross-talk — everyone acking the plan)
[08:45] Diego: a couple of technical clarifications — is StrataForge expecting to route tenant tokens to Redwood (i.e., us doing multi-tenant routing) or will StrataForge proxy and invoice?
[08:57] Maya: likely we'll proxy and invoice — customers will see StrataForge in billing. but for compliance we may need per-tenant isolation, so metadata per request is required.
[09:12] Diego: okay we'll expose per-tenant headers and tokenization so that you can do billing and isolation.
[09:20] Ava: timeline — what are you looking for?
[09:23] Maya: we'd like a pilot with 3 customers in Q1 and general availability for partner onramp by late Q2.
[09:30] Ava: doable. pilot first then scale.
[09:33] Tomás: can we run agentless benchmarks? some customers don't want code install.
[09:39] Diego: yes we have a remote harness that hits endpoints with synthetic payloads; but for best numbers we prefer a small agent to prime KV caches.
[09:51] Elise: any known regulatory blockers for EU customers?
[09:55] Diego: data residency and logging retention policies are the usual items; we have region-locked storage and retention controls.
[10:05] Jonah: next steps recap please?
[10:08] Ava: quick recap — i will send partner deck, nda, pricing template, and pilot SOW. diego will send benchmark harness and sample workloads. elise will confirm compliance artifacts access. tomás will share infra topology and preferred SKUs. schedule deep dive for network/VPC next week.
[10:28] Maya: sounds good. one more thing — competitor concerns: some partners already work with CloudSmith and they ask about migration costs. how do you make switching low friction?
[10:43] Ava: migration playbook — SDK compatibility, a traffic split for canary, and an import tool for billing mapping. we'll include that in the deck.
[10:56] (short pause)
[11:05] Diego: on the technical deep-dive we'll validate the KV cache sizes, continuous batching windows, and expected tokenization overheads. we'll also run a small end-to-end with your A100 pool.
[11:20] Tomás: about telemetry — do you provide per-request traces?
[11:24] Diego: yes tracing and token-level latency breakdowns. we can give a temporary team invite to console for viewing.
[11:33] Elise: for the NDA and SOC2 access, we will need the SOC2 pdf and contact for auditors.
[11:39] Ava: I'll include SOC2 and the auditor contact in the package.
[11:44] Jonah: question — for reseller billing, does Redwood support a consolidated monthly invoice or monthly per-tenant?
[11:52] Ava: we can do both. most partners want consolidated with per-tenant line items.
[11:58] Maya: ok great. anything else?
[12:02] (background noise, someone typing)
[12:10] Ava: thanks all — will follow up with the docs and we should lock the deep-dive time.
[12:16] Maya: thanks everyone, excited to kick this off.
[12:20] Tomás: thanks.
[12:22] Elise: bye.

Meeting end: 15:56 UTC approx.

Notes on transcript: occasional botched proper nouns (H1O0 = H100, Redwood Dedicate = Redwood Dedicated) and minor ASR errors.
